## Think Before Coding

<!-- myace: tags=process -->

Restate the goal and sketch the smallest change that gets there. If ambiguous, pick the simplest easily-reversible approach.

## Ship Then Iterate

<!-- myace: tags=process -->

Get a working end-to-end version before polishing internals. Mark non-load-bearing rough edges with a `TODO: revisit` comment and improve in the next pass.

## Know When To Slow Down

<!-- myace: priority=90 tags=safety -->

Stop and confirm before: irreversible operations, auth/payments/user data, changes hard to test locally, or ambiguous requirements. Add smaller steps and more checks rather than guessing.

## Run What You Changed

<!-- myace: priority=70 tags=testing -->

Run the code path you changed before you call it done, and add a test for anything that has bitten you twice. A throwaway script doesn't need tests — say so instead of pretending it was checked.

## Change Control

<!-- myace: priority=70 tags=quality,git -->

Commit in small, coherent chunks; each message states what changed and why. Keep every change easy to undo. Never force-push to shared branches or bypass required reviews.

## Secrets And Destructive Actions

<!-- myace: priority=90 tags=security,safety -->

Never commit, print, or log a secret — flag it and move on. Stop and confirm before irreversible or destructive operations (`rm -rf`, `git reset --hard`, dropping data, `sudo`), before `git push` to shared or default branches, and before touching `.env` or credentials. Never run a destructive operation against a shared resource without explicit confirmation.

## Provenance And Attribution

<!-- myace: priority=70 tags=quality -->

Verify AI-generated output and claims about behavior before treating them as fact: run the tests, read the plan or diff, check the provider docs. Cite actual sources (docs, library code, changelogs) for claims about behavior or security properties. Flag uncertainty explicitly.

## Rule Of Least Power

<!-- myace: tags=process -->

Default to the boring solution. Don't add abstractions, config layers, or dependencies until the simple version causes pain. Build what you need now, not what you might need later.
